entities.summary:
Hugh de Balsham was a medieval English bishop, consecrated as bishop of Ely in 1261. He played a significant role in the English Reformation, supporting the ideas of John Wycliffe and William Tyndale. De Balsham's influence extended to the establishment of the Church of England, with his successor, Thomas Arundel, serving as Archbishop of Canterbury. The bishop's leadership and theological stance contributed to the growth of English Protestantism. Hugh de Balsham's legacy can be seen in the development of the English Reformation and the Church of England.

Born in 1235, de Balsham was the son of a noble family and received a classical education at Oxford University. He became a cleric and was elected as the Bishop of Norwich before his appointment as bishop of Ely. De Balsham's tenure as bishop was marked by his efforts to reform the church and promote the use of the vernacular language in worship.

De Balsham died on June 23, 1286, at the age of 51, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Church of England and the English Reformation.

In his later years, de Balsham was known for his strong support of the English monarchy, which contributed to the strengthening of the institution.

One notable quote from de Balsham reflects his commitment to the English Reformation: 'The Church of England shall be a holy and catholic church, with the authority of the Holy Spirit.'
